messages:
Ryn: Quick sync — saw a 504 yesterday during a private->hosted fallback. Not panicked but think our current handoff timing is underspecified across hosting modes. Need a short design convo on explicit grace periods, circuit timings, and observable signals we can rely on.

Katie: Which path was exercised? private->hosted or hosted->dedicated?

Ryn: private->hosted. Sequence: request routed to private, control-plane decided to fallback to hosted because private pool hit eviction threshold. The runtime started teardown, we saw inflight streams drop and then 504s when routing cutover happened.

Ryn: Minimal log snippet: ```
2026-03-17T18:02:12Z controlplane: schedule fallback for tenant=acme reason=capacity
2026-03-17T18:02:14Z runtime: begin drain connections target=private-node-23
2026-03-17T18:02:15Z router: update route -> hosted-variant
2026-03-17T18:02:18Z proxy: stream reset, err=connection_aborted
2026-03-17T18:02:25Z request: 504 gateway timeout
```

Jon: Hmm. That looks like the router moved before the runtime finished KV cache handshake/drain. We never defined an inter-mode "grace period" contract. Right now it's implicit and differs by adapter.

Sophie: +1. We need an explicit 3-phase handshake for mode switch: PROBE (is target reachable & warmed?), QUIESCE/DRAIN (allow inflight requests to finish + flush KV caches), SWITCH (move traffic). Timings per phase should be policy-driven but have sane defaults.

Katie: What defaults are we thinking? Any numbers to start experiments with?

Jon: Proposal sketch: PROBE=5s (connect + warm check), DRAIN=30s for hosted<->dedicated, 60s for private->hosted (private can have longer cold starts), SWITCH=instant after DRAIN. Provide config knobs per-tenant and per-route.

Sophie: Numbers ok as starting point, but drain should be adaptive: if KV cache size > X or active streams > Y, extend drain. Otherwise fixed 30s/60s is wasteful and adds latency/cost. Also add a graceful fallback timeout: if drain doesn't finish within max_drain (e.g., 120s), proceed with best-effort switch and emit high-severity alert.

Ryn: Agree on adaptive drain + max cap. Need to define what signals the runtime exposes: active_stream_count, kv_cache_bytes, last_acked_token_index, and a 'drain_complete' boolean. Router picks up drain_complete before switching.

Jon: Important: compatibility. Old adapters might not emit drain_complete. We should have a compatibility mode: if adapter doesn't report signals, fall back to conservative fixed drains (e.g., 90s). But that will be opt-in during rollout.

Katie: For rollout, we should feature-flag the new handshake in controlplane, and a plugin version check for adapters. Also add telemetry: histograms for PROBE, DRAIN, SWITCH durations and error counts.

deploy-bot: Incident 2026-03-17-504 detected for tenant=acme at 2026-03-17T18:02:25Z — auto-created ticket #INC-4127 :rotating_light:

Sophie: Ops question — what about clients with long streaming connections? We need a deprecation/redirect strategy or a connection migration. Some streams can't be easily re-established.

Jon: For streams we can attempt a proxy-level connection handoff if the runtime supports session migration, otherwise we should advertise per-route metadata indicating "no-migrate" and skip fallback for those routes unless forced.

Ryn: I suggest the initial RFC covers: handshake phases, minimal signal set (active_stream_count, kv_cache_bytes, drain_complete), default timings, adaptive algorithms, compatibility mode, rollout/feature flag plan, and telemetry + alert thresholds.

Katie: I'll own the RFC + rollout plan. ETA EOW for a draft? I can include a sample controlplane config like: ```yaml
fallback_policy:
  probe_timeout: 5s
  drain_policy:
    default: 30s
    private_override: 60s
    adaptive: true
    max_drain: 120s
  compatibility_fallback: 90s
```

Sophie: Please include perf/cost impact section — longer drains mean slower failovers and potentially higher bill for reserved capacity. Also include a canary traffic experiment to validate.

Jon: Also add tests: unit tests for handshake state machine, integration test with adapter shim that simulates missing signals, and a chaos test that forces evictions during drain.

Ryn: Action items: Katie draft RFC (due EOW), Jon adds runtime signal API spec snippet, Sophie writes testing + perf checklist, I'll add router gating changes and metric names. We'll sync Thurs 11am to approve RFC for alpha rollout.

Sophie: thumbs up :+1:

Katie: noted, will ping folks when draft is up.

Ryn: Thanks all — this should prevent another 504 surprise and make mode transitions predictable.
